newsitem.title: USA: New Holland offering boosts IPOs.
newsitem.headline: New Holland offering boosts IPOs.

text.p: Initial public offerings of the stock of global companies in the United States have hit a new all-time high this year, a record $7.2 billion, toppling the 1994 record of $6.9 billion.
Friday's billion dollar market debut of New Holland NV pushed the dollar volume of international IPOs over the top, according to Securities Data Co.
With Europe's largest ever stock issue due later this month, the partial privatisation of Deutsche Telekom, 1996 could be in the record books for some time.

"There's a growing presence of companies coming here for capital instead of their own backyards ... it's the dollars, the liquidity and the institutional and fund managers, who can tuck these shares away," said Richard Peterson, spokesman for Securities Data.

The biggest international deals so far this year were Swedish truck maker Scania's $2.7 billion offering, British mobile telephone group Orange Plc's $1.02 billion market debut and Telefonica del Peru $1.01 billion deal.

"Companies come here because valuations and liquidity are much better than in Europe, plus the size of the U.S. market drives people here," said Manish Shah, editor of the IPO Maven. "Also, European investors are much more conservative and not willing to finance venture capital operations. So many companies would never be able to go public here."
Italian car-maker Fiat SpA sold 30 percent of its New Holland unit, which makes agricultural machinery, in a $999.8 million offering of 53.5 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Germany's national telecommunications company Deutsche Telekom is planning a blockbuster multi-billion dollar IPO of 500 million shares to be offered in a range of 25 to 30 marks each.
Shah was not enthusiastic about the quality of the offering, but said it could perform well due to the strong backing of the German government.
"The company has huge debt, poor service, and a way to go in terms of catching up with quality technology," he said.

He said he expects this week's offerings to be somewhat mediocre, with SeaChange International Inc. the best bet for long-term investors. The company provides video-on-demand services and allows cable companies to store and manage their archives.

Initial public offerings, both domestic and international, hit record levels in October according to IPO Aftermarket editor John Fitzgibbon. He said 105 new issues priced in October, surpassing the May 1996 record of 97.
